newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end flat as early gains slashed.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end flat as early gains slashed.

text.p: SPI Futures 2524 -16 US 30yr cl 6.89 -0.05
10yrbond futs 92.315 -0.005 Gold NY 348.05 Lon fix 345.85
S&P500(Globex) 829.65 steady NZSE40 2300.20 -12.05
*Stocks end little changed, early gains wiped out as futures weigh on market in afternoon. Vol 354.71 million, value A$795.34 million, 1,093 stocks traded, 360 steady, 409 up, 324 down.
The Australian share market ended a choppy day's trade little changed on Monday with a falling afternoon futures market wiping out early record-breaking gains.

The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 1.2 points lower at 2,524.8 having touched a record high of 2,538 mid-morning, surpassing the previous record high of 2,528.1 reached last Friday. The June share price index futures were 16 points down at 2,524, a wafer thin 0.8 discount to the underlying index.
The strong start failed to last as nerves ahead of Tuesday's Federal budget seemed to get the better of traders although activity was moderate rather than heavy.
"The futures lost their nerve in the afternoon," said a Sydney-based broker, noting that most had not expected much movement ahead of the government's second budget.
"Volumes are okay but nothing sensational. We called it with only five or so points in it at best and that is the way it has ended up."

Definitive reasons for the afternoon's losses proved elusive with brokers saying they could only put it down to investors taking a defensive stance ahead of tomorrow night's release of the 1997/98 fiscal programme.
"The budget was always likely to take some (traders) out but I'm not expecting big surprises tomorrow," the broker said.
Others agreed, suggesting the market had wandered back to where its started with few discernible underlying influences.

"It just seemed to run out of puff and lost its way a bit," said head of institutions at Ord Minnett, Eric Gale, echoing the call that few shocks were expected from Treasurer Costello's second budget.
"I don't know that the market is too budget-conscious. It's been a fair while since the budget was a document full of surprises."

Among individual stocks building materials, sugar and aluminium group CSR was the feature, posting a sharply lower full year net profit of A$212 million, citing a continued subdued housing industry for the softer result.
Its shares ended just A$0.007 lower at A$4.763 with brokers suggesting the result had failed to surprise.
"The bottom line wasn't too far away from what the market was looking at," Gale said.
Furniture retailer Freedom Furniture reported a sharply higher half year net profit of A$4.65 million and declared a interim dividend of 3.5 cents per share.
Freedom shares closed at a record high A$1.588.

Gold miners Acacia Resources, up nine cents to A$2.04, Plutonic Resources, up 15 cents to A$5.10, and Sons of Gwalia, up 17 at A$5.63, were the pick of the precious metals miners boosted by the stronger gold price.

Elsewhere among the resources, West-Australia-based miner St Barbara featured early with 10.6 million shares traded, the bulk of it in one line of 10.35 million shares specialled through Porter Western at a price of 72 cents per share. St Barbara shares ended 3.7 cents higher at 66 cents.
